propositions: The hardening byte-equivalence oracle launches 884 copied legacy Pandoc subprocesses that share mutable production conversion constants with the real production path, allowing a production format mutation to pass undetected when both sides move identically.

Replacing the copied legacy subprocess with an immutable fixture of expected outputs keyed by platform-specific Pandoc binary SHA-256 eliminates 884 subprocesses and 32.3 seconds from per-change test time while preserving all 884 real production Pandoc invocations.

The schema must record both the generating Pandoc version and platform-specific binary fingerprint map (darwin-arm64 and linux-x86_64) with platform-keyed lookup to prevent cross-platform CI rejection.
A deterministic regeneration script and installed version/platform/hash drift assertion must fail closed when Pandoc provenance changes or an unsupported platform is encountered.
